name: bus_power_tps2121
title: Bus power into the Pi
purpose: 5 V from the spacecraft bus to the Pi's 5 V pins through a TPS2121 (reverse current blocking, current limit), as the HAT guide's back-power diode

sources.title: TI TPS2120/TPS2121 priority power mux (SLVSEA3F)
sources.licence: TI datasheet; link and quotes only
sources.read: p1, p4-5 pin functions, electrical characteristics (ILM), 9.3.2 current limit, 10.2 design example (CSS), 11 power supply, 12 layout

sources.title: raspberrypi/hats: designguide.md and README.md
sources.licence: Raspberry Pi documentation (repository marked deprecated); link and quotes only

parts.quote: "TPS2121 VQFN-HR (12) 56 mΩ 4.5 A"; pins OUT 1, 8; IN2 2; CP2 3; OV2 4; OV1 5; PR1 6; IN1 7; ST 9; ILIM 10; SS 11; GND 12; "FAST REVERSE CURRENT BLOCKING (RCB)". hatguide: "Implement a duplicate power safety diode before the HAT 5V net"; "the Raspberry Pi 3B+, 4B, Zero and ZeroW **do not** include an input ZVD"; footprint: KiCad's Texas_VQFN-HR-12_2x2.5mm_P0.5mm with our 3D model (KiCad has none), from TI's RUX0012A outline
parts.pin_types_why: tps2121 p5: ST "Status output indicating which channel is selected. Connect to GND if not required."; 9.3: "If this feature is not required, the ST pin can be connected to GND." The electrical table lists an ST pull-up resistance (RST), so grounding it is the datasheet's own use, not an output fighting ground.

parts.quote: "ILM = 65.2 / RILM^0.861" (RILM in kΩ, 18-100 kΩ): 30.1 kΩ gives 3.5 A; table: "RILM = 29.8kΩ … 3 3.5 4 A". Above the guide's "supply 5V at 2.5A", within the XH connector's 3 A
"a CSS capacitance of 100 nF will provide a slew rate of 780V/S (typical)", limiting inrush "below 100 mA in a typical application"

"Bypass capacitors on these pins should be placed as close to the device as possible. Low ESR ceramic capacitors with X5R or X7R dielectric"; "where there are long cables … a large capacitance can be used near the input". Value estimated: the datasheet gives none
"To avoid output voltage drop, the capacitance on OUT can be increased". Value estimated: the datasheet gives none

layout.rules: tps2121 12.1: "Use short wide traces for input and output planes. For high current applications place vias under input and output pins". PR1, CP2, OV1, OV2 and ST to GND: "Connect to GND if not required" (p4-5). IN1 and IN2 pads joined under the chip, OUT pads likewise, 0.4 mm (the pads are 0.4 mm tall, 0.3 mm apart); 1.0 mm once clear of the pads, to C2 (VBUS) and C3 (+5V).

open_questions: R1 sets the limit by the datasheet's equation (30.1 kΩ is not in its table; 29.8 kΩ is).

IN2 is tied to IN1 (one supply on both channels) so no input floats; the datasheet's single-supply use ("If only one input voltage is valid … then that input will power the output") doesn't say what to do with the unused input. Check with TI's documents before ordering.
C2 and C3 values are estimates; the datasheet asks for low-ESR X5R/X7R but gives no value.
No TVS or fuse on the bus input: the HAT guide's diagram shows a polyfuse on the Pi side only; bus protection is a spacecraft-level choice still open.
